segments: ... al-Aziz went to Egypt,
and al-Adil remained in Damascus,
as if on behalf of al-Malik al-Aziz,
while the general command was his own,
and to the other belonged the title alone.
Many times al-Malik al-Zahir, the lord of Aleppo, sent to al-Malik al-Afdal, saying to him:
"Do not trust al-Adil,
because no good will come to us from him.
For I know him better than you do.
For even though he is the uncle of all of us,
yet I am his son-in-law.
And if I knew that he had compassion for us,
it would be more fitting for me to attach myself to him, or for you."
And al-Afdal would reply:
"Your opinion is not right;
this man is in the place of our father,
and how could he harm us?" And in the year 593
of the Arabs (1197 AD):
al-Adil attacked the Franks again,
as the peace had been dissolved by the death of the king of England {OCR?} and of Saladin.
And he went and encamped against Jaffa and took it by battle.
Then the Franks of the seacoast sent to those inland and said:
"If you do not come to our aid quickly,
the Arabs will rule over the entire seacoast."
And the Franks from inland sent a great number of forces,
and they appointed as their head a man of the clergy who was called chancellor (chancellor?);
and they set out and encamped against Tibnin,
and waged a fierce battle against it.
And when they were close to taking it,
the report reached them
that Henry, the Count of Acre, had fallen from a high place and died.
And since they had no king left,
they withdrew from the battle.
And they sent and brought the lord of Cyprus,
and gave him the wife of Henry.
And when al-Adil heard,
he sent to him and made peace on the condition
that Beirut should belong to the Franks,
and Tibnin to the Arabs.
And the Franks abandoned Tibnin and left.
And in that same year died Malikshah, the son of Khwarazmshah Tekish, in the land of Nishapur (in Nishapur);
and Qutb al-Din Muhammad arose after him,
although the leadership rightfully belonged to his brother Hindu Khan according to their father's will,
and not to him.
And at this same time also died Sayf al-Din al-Islam Tughtekin, the son of Ayyub,
the brother of Saladin,
he who had ruled over the land of Yemen;
and his son Ismail arose in his place.
